note: All four directives were published as `references`, which is the label for a dependency that has no import statement — and the store's `imports` binding, which 16 analyzers emit and this one did not, never saw one. `import` IS the language word for the ontology word, and ERLANG made the identical correction for `-import(lists, [map/2])` on the neighbouring BEAM language (ERD41). The other three keep `references` and the family contract they were written for: `use` injects a module's code, `require` permits its macros to expand, `alias` renames a module — none brings a name into unqualified scope. Both directions are pinned (an import is not a reference, a use is not an import) because a move that emits BOTH labels would satisfy either assertion. The `:only` call-resolution rule (ELXD17) is unchanged: `thing(x)` still resolves through `import Onto.Narrow, only: [thing: 1]`. `meta.evidenceClass` distinguishes `import_directive` from `module_directive`, so the reason a dependency edge exists is a queryable number and not a vibe (honesty §4.3).

expectRelationships.note: the emission was an unqualified local call; the post-walk :only-import resolution named the remote target, and the reason code is re-stated to match the published edge (honesty §4.1)

forbidRelationships.note: EX-EX13: `defmacro import(module, opts)` is a declaration head, not an import statement — the target would be the macro's own parameter name, which is not a module and is never a stored symbol
EX-EX13: the same shape for `defmacro require(module)`
